SENIOR PROJECT MANAGER | Hydrology, Hydraulics, Master Planning and Design
ICON Engineering · Centennial, CO

ICON Engineering is a Denver area civil engineering consulting firm specializing in water resources, stormwater and floodplain management. We are known for solving complex watershed and community infrastructure projects with engineering excellence. We are seeking a Senior Project Manager to lead multi-disciplinary teams through hydrologic and hydraulic modeling, floodplain and stormwater studies, and design projects as well as build client relationships in these practice areas. The ideal candidate brings genuine enthusiasm for natural resources, watersheds and the communities these projects serve.

- Technical duties including H&H modeling oversight, floodplain and stormwater studies, QA/QC for design, and engineering support for construction.
- Project management duties including project scope, schedule and budget development and monitoring; preparing invoices for client billing; team workload planning; leading routine group meetings; participating in project manager meetings, and mentoring staff.
- Champion relationships and business development with clients. Assist with client communication, writing proposals for project pursuits and contract negotiations.
- Prepare outreach materials, lead meetings, and present technical information to clients.
- Lead teams with surveyors, landscape architects, planners, ecologists and others to deliver high quality project deliverables.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS
- Bachelor's degree in civil engineering with emphasis in water resources or an environmental field
- PE designation
- More than 10 years of full-time experience in water resource engineering and at least 5 years in a project management capacity.
- Ability to participate in a hybrid working environment that will require an in-person presence (Centennial Office)
- Experience working in a team environment. Excellent communication skills.
- Familiarity with EPA SWMM, CUHP, HEC RAS, 2D models, AutoCAD Civil 3D, ESRI, Microsoft

ADDITIONAL DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS
- Master's Degree in Civil Engineering with emphasis in water resources
- CFM certification
- MHFD and other local agency experience in the Denver, CO area

BENEFITS/ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
- ICON offers a competitive compensation package that includes paid time off, holiday pay, health/dental/vision insurance, 401k, I-Coin Performance Bonus Program, staff social events, training / field visits, internal committees, career development, and much more!
- ICON offers a flexible work week and hybrid work environments.
- Opportunity to grow into firm leadership role
- Salary range for this position is $110k to $180k, dependent on experience. All inquiries will be handled confidentially.
- Position may require field site visits and occasional travel.

description:
Project Engineer | Specialty: Stormwater, Floodplain, and Stream Restoration Project Engineer (EI)
ICON Engineering · Fort Collins, CO

ICON Engineering is seeking a civil or environmental engineer to join our Northern Colorado Team. This Team enjoys working on a wide range of stormwater analysis and design projects including storm drainage systems, water quality BMPs, flood mitigation, and stream restoration located in Northern Colorado. These projects are often multi-disciplinary and exemplify all aspects of stormwater and civil infrastructure design. Project examples may include: technical floodplain analysis using 1D and 2D HECRAS; hydrology studies using HEC-HMS, HEC-SSP, or CUHP; design of stormwater systems and stream restoration projects using EPA-SWMM and Civil3D; major drainageway floodplain studies and FEMA map revision preparation using ArcGIS; and water quality improvement design. Strong communication and technical writing skills are required for project documentation and collaboration with project teams and clients. The person who fills this position will assist over the life cycle of these projects, from assessment, to planning, design, permitting, and construction. The ideal candidate will have a passion for stormwater management, flood mitigation, streams, rivers, and watersheds and a desire to grow in their career. A highly qualified candidate will bring experience in hydrologic and hydraulic analyses using the computer programs noted above.

This position is located in Fort Collins, CO. The position is hybrid but regular business hours and working 3-4 days per week in-office is expected. The position will also include occasional field work/ site visits generally in Northern Colorado/ along Colorado's Front Range. The successful candidate will collaborate with members of ICON's Northern Colorado Team and strong teamwork/ interpersonal skills are essential.

ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES
- Analyze stormwater and flood mitigation infrastructure
- Study watersheds, analyze basin characteristics, precipitation, and runoff volumes
- Design storm drains, detention/water quality systems, channels, and natural drainage systems
- Floodplain studies and related FEMA flood mapping
- Stormwater Management, Erosion and Sediment Control, and Master Planning studies
- Design stream restoration projects
- Construction plan development
- Collaborate with design team
- Project documentation
- Attend meetings, and present technical information to clients
- Work under the guidance and supervision from ICON's Project Management Team

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS
- Bachelor's and/or Master's Degree in civil or environmental engineering
- Engineering Intern (EI) or ability to obtain within 6 months
- 0 to 2 years of civil or water resources engineering experience
- Willingness to learn new software programs
- Willingness to ask questions, seek instruction, and problem solve
- Ability to participate in a small team, collaborative, hybrid working environment

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
- Experience with HEC-RAS, EPA SWMM, and other hydraulic modeling software
- Experience with HEC-HMS, CUHP, and other hydrologic modeling software
- Experience with ArcGIS
- Experience with AutoCAD
- Experience with FEMA floodplain studies and/or storm sewer design projects

BENEFITS / ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
- ICON offers a competitive compensation package that includes paid time off, holiday pay, health/dental/vision insurance, 401k, I-Coin Performance Bonus Program, staff social events, training, career development, and much more!
- Salary range for this position is $68k to $83k, depending on experience. All inquiries will be handled confidentially.

Project Manager I/II - Drainage
City of Greenwood Village · Greenwood Village, CO
Department: Public Works or Parks, Trails & Recreation · Supervisor: Senior Project Manager · Full-time/salaried

FULL SALARY RANGE
- Project Manager I - $36.20 - $54.11
- Project Manager II - $42.65 - $63.64

BENEFITS
Health, dental, and vision insurance; life and AD&D insurance; disability insurance; retirement plans; employee assistance programs; paid training; education reimbursement; vacation and sick leave accrual; 11 paid holidays.

REMOTE/HYBRID: Typical schedules are in-office Monday through Friday. Remote and flexible scheduling may be discussed upon hire and with supervisor approval.
RELOCATION: This position is located in Greenwood Village, Colorado. Relocation assistance is not provided.

About the Role
As a Project Manager I/II, you will provide engineering expertise supporting transportation, drainage, parks, and construction initiatives throughout Greenwood Village. You'll manage capital improvement projects from conception through completion, perform engineering studies, analyze data, review plans, conduct inspections, collaborate with contractors and engineers, support residents, and ensure infrastructure improvements meet City standards for safety, functionality, and environmental stewardship.

Position Levels
- Project Manager I: Entry-level professional engineering role suitable for candidates with foundational knowledge and limited or no directly related experience.
- Project Manager II: Journey-level engineering role responsible for the full spectrum of complex engineering duties, project management responsibilities, and independent work within assigned programs.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities
A. Civil Engineering Functions
- Conduct engineering studies on assigned projects; perform civil engineering cost analyses; prepare and/or review computations, preliminary layouts and design work from field and survey data
- Perform engineering design work, including researching data and determining design criteria per required standards and codes; prepare calculations, sketches, plans, specifications and estimates
- Review engineering and architectural drawings involving drainage, parks, roads, utilities, and traffic control devices
- Prepare engineering plans, charts, and graphs from rough design sketches and field notes
- Collaborate and confer with engineers, architects, and contractors; present engineering analysis to the public, City Council, and commissions
- Perform field inspections to verify construction improvement accuracy
- Manage contracts or projects; review reports for conformance to contracts, approved plans, agency regulations, and engineering standards; monitor schedules, change orders, costs, and regulatory compliance
- Assist with review of development applications, including civil plans, grading plans, preliminary plats, and final plats
B. Project Manager on Capital Improvement Projects
- Manage and administer capital improvement projects from design to completion; review consultant and contractor work; recommend and approve payment processing
- Review and approve design, prepare requests for proposals, take bids for construction, and recommend award
- Prepare contract documents; initiate change orders
- Perform or direct construction inspection to ensure public improvements conform to City codes and approved plans
- Assist in developing and administering program budget, procedures and goals; develop Capital Improvement Program projects
- Prepare proposals; manage contracts; recommend consultant selection; negotiate consultant fees
- Work with citizens to develop project scopes; present projects at public meetings, City Council and Commissions
- Manage CIP project development and budget; coordinate external funding, design, construction, intergovernmental agreements, and public involvement
C. Environmental/Drainage Engineering Functions
- Ensure water quality and adequate drainage facilities per Federal, state and local regulations, including EPA and CDPHE Water Quality Control Division
- Review City and private development plans and drainage reports for conformance with the Greenwood Village Drainage Criteria Manual
- Provide engineering support on drainage projects; prepare designs and specifications
- Assist with floodplain administration and direct Code Enforcement Officers on grading and drainage violations
D. Roadway Engineering Functions
- Develop specifications, cost estimates and scope for pavement reconstruction, rehabilitation, preservation, trails and maintenance contracts
- Oversee infrastructure inventory and rating
E. Traffic Engineering Functions
- Traffic studies, radar speed surveys, accident data analysis, traffic counts; review street improvement plans, signing and striping
F. Parks Engineering Functions
- Groundwater well and irrigation water rights reports; in-house AutoCAD designs for retaining walls, irrigation, well adjustments and trail modifications; civil details for park facility renovations
G. Supervisory Responsibilities
- Plan, prioritize and review work of assigned personnel; schedules and resources; staff selection, training, performance assessments, coaching
H. Miscellaneous Administrative Functions
- Recommendations to City Manager, departments, Commissions and City Council; professional group meetings; respond to citizen requests; other duties as assigned

Required Skills & Qualifications
Project Manager I:
- Knowledge of civil engineering principles, mathematics, design, and construction practices
- Ability to learn engineering-specific terminology, codes, regulations, and best management practices
- Ability to perform technical research, solve engineering problems, and prepare designs under supervision
- Proficiency with office software and computer engineering systems
- Strong communication and interpersonal skills
Project Manager II (includes PM I skills plus):
- Comprehensive understanding of engineering principles and practices in civil, environmental, or traffic engineering
- Experience with pavement design, construction methods, materials testing, and quality assurance
- Knowledge of project management, municipal budgeting, and supervision
- Ability to independently design, review, and modify engineering plans and specifications
- Ability to manage capital improvement projects and supervise assigned personnel

Education & Experience Requirements
Project Manager I:
- Bachelor's degree in civil engineering, environmental engineering, traffic engineering, or related field
- No experience required
- Valid Colorado driver's license or ability to obtain
Project Manager II:
- Three years of responsible civil, environmental, or traffic engineering experience
- Professional Engineer registration, Engineering Intern certificate, Master's degree, Certified Landscape Architect, PMP certification, or AICP certification
- Valid Colorado driver's license or ability to obtain

Working Conditions
Work occurs both indoors and outdoors, with exposure to varying weather conditions. Interaction with City staff and the public is frequent. May require evening and weekend work.

Apply by 2:00pm, Friday, November 13, 2026. Applications are reviewed as received; the posting may close without notice once a qualified candidate is identified.
